name: ADI Site Bridge
author: Adiuvo

sections.description:
ADI Site Bridge connects your site to ADI (Adiuvo Digital Intelligence), the desktop assistant from Adiuvo.

Ask ADI “change the hours heading to Winter Hours” and it finds the right field, shows you the change, waits for your approval, makes it, and keeps a restore point.

The plugin is the site’s side of the connection: you need ADI on your computer to use it (see External services below). Nothing on the site is locked or limited: everything the plugin can do is available to any connection you create.

It works with the way your site is built:

  • Classic editor and page builders that use shortcodes (WPBakery, Divi, Avada): text between shortcodes.
  • Block editor (Gutenberg): paragraphs, headings, lists, buttons, images, custom HTML.
  • Elementor: widgets by their Elementor id (headings, text, buttons, images, icon boxes, lists, accordions, tabs).
  • Advanced Custom Fields (ACF PRO, ACF, Secure Custom Fields): fields, groups, repeaters, flexible content sections, and options pages such as Site Settings.
  • WooCommerce: simple products’ regular and sale prices (always shown with your store currency), sale dates, SKU and stock; products’ categories and tags (existing ones), product image and gallery (Media Library images), and simple products’ own attribute values, all through WooCommerce’s own product API. Variable products: each variation’s prices (with your store currency), sale dates, SKU, stock, enabled/disabled and image, one change at a time; variations are never added or removed and their attributes never change.

What it never does:

  • It never changes SEO titles, meta descriptions, social previews or schema (those stay with your SEO tool).
  • It never adds, removes or reorders sections, blocks or widgets; never changes page addresses; never deletes permanently.
  • It never acts beyond the permissions of the WordPress user you choose.
  • It never changes store settings (currency, tax, shipping), orders, customers, coupons or payments.
  • It never changes WordPress’s own settings, the theme, plugins, users, styling, Customizer or widgets: it edits content only (pages, posts, products and their fields, including the fields of ACF options pages), whatever the connection’s WordPress role.

ADI Site Bridge Pro

A second edition, ADI Site Bridge Pro, adds page and site styling, the theme’s Customizer settings and widget editing. It is free, is not hosted on WordPress.org, and is installed by hand from adiuvo.ca. The two editions share their connections and restore points; run one or the other.

External services

This plugin connects your site to ADI, a desktop application made by Adiuvo (https://adiuvo.ca).

  • What the plugin sends, and when: the plugin makes no outgoing connection to Adiuvo or any AI service for this. It waits for requests. When you create a connection (Settings → ADI Bridge) and paste its token into ADI, ADI connects to this site’s REST API over HTTPS, as the WordPress user you chose. It reads the content it is asked about (pages, posts, products and their fields) and changes it only after you approve each change in ADI. Requests to your site come only from the ADI application on that computer, never from an Adiuvo server, and the connection token is kept on that computer. A job can be started from the owner’s paired phone: it runs in ADI on the computer, and each change still needs approval.
  • What ADI tells Adiuvo about the site: ADI reports the site’s domain, its label in ADI, whether it is switched on, the number of pages, posts and drafts, and the WordPress and plugin versions to the Adiuvo account ADI is logged in to (app.adiuvo.ca), so the account can list its connected sites. The token and the site’s content are not part of that.
  • Where that content goes: the content ADI reads is shown on your computer, and may be sent by ADI to the AI provider the ADI user chose (for example Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, or a model running on that computer) so it can answer and propose changes. Which provider is used, and under which terms, is set in ADI, not on this site.
  • Turning it off: revoke the connection in Settings → ADI Bridge, or deactivate the plugin. Nothing is sent from the site without a valid connection token.

Adiuvo Terms of Service: https://adiuvo.ca/terms
Adiuvo Privacy Policy: https://adiuvo.ca/privacy

Security

  • Tokens are stored only as hashes and can be revoked any time (Settings → ADI Bridge → Revoke); revoking takes effect immediately.
  • Every request runs as the chosen WordPress user, so WordPress’s own permissions apply. Users without full HTML rights can’t save embeds or scripts through ADI either.
  • Pages open in the WordPress editor are not changed (your next save would overwrite ADI’s change).
  • Every change keeps a restore point (the 20 most recent per page); ADI can put a page back in one step.
  • Browser requests from other sites are refused.
  • The site answers ADI over https only. A request over plain http is refused whether or not its token is valid, and a site without https cannot create a connection (a site on your own computer, at localhost, is the one exception).
  • Use https all the way to your server. A CDN mode that encrypts only between the visitor and the CDN (Cloudflare’s “Flexible” mode) still sends the token over the last leg unencrypted.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “ADI Site Bridge”, then install and activate it.
  2. Go to Settings → ADI Bridge → New connection. Give it a name and choose the WordPress user ADI acts as. A dedicated Editor account is recommended, not an administrator: the bridge itself can only read, edit, publish or trash content, and can’t add scripts, embeds (iframes), forms, event handlers or javascript: links through ADI, whatever the role (markup already on a page is left as it is), but whoever holds the token can change anything that user can edit.
    On a WooCommerce store, products need WooCommerce’s product permissions: use a dedicated Shop Manager account (or an Editor whose role has been given WooCommerce’s product permissions).
  3. Copy the token shown (it is shown only once) and the site address.
  4. In ADI: Settings → Connections → WordPress Site → paste the address and the token → Connect.
sections.faq:
Do I need ADI?

Yes. This plugin is the site’s side of the connection; ADI, Adiuvo’s desktop assistant, is what you talk to. Without a connection from ADI the plugin does nothing except show its settings page. ADI is available from adiuvo.ca.

Is the plugin free?

Yes. The plugin is free and complete: it has no paid version, no licence key and no locked features. ADI itself is a separate desktop application that needs an Adiuvo subscription.

Which WordPress user should ADI act as?

A dedicated Editor account (Users → Add New). Every request runs as that user, so WordPress’s own permissions apply. A WooCommerce store needs a Shop Manager (or an Editor given WooCommerce’s product permissions) for product changes.

ADI says the token was refused, but it is correct

If Last used stays at “never”, your host may strip the Authorization header before WordPress sees it. Update ADI first: version 1.1.28 and later also send the token in a header hosts leave alone. On an older ADI, on Apache, add this line near the top of .htaccess:

SetEnvIf Authorization "(.*)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1

How do I undo a change?

Ask ADI to put it back: every change keeps a restore point (the 20 most recent per page).

How do I disconnect ADI?

Settings → ADI Bridge → Revoke. Revoking takes effect immediately.
Deleting the plugin removes every connection token.
sections.changelog:
0.2.1

  • First release in the WordPress.org plugin directory.
  • This edition edits content only. Page and site styling, Customizer settings and widget editing are not part of it.
  • Everything the plugin stores or registers now uses the prefix adibridge. Connections and restore points from earlier versions are carried over the first time the site loads.
  • For developers: the plugin’s hooks are renamed from adi_bridge_… to adibridge_…. Code that uses the old names must be updated.
  • The readme says what ADI reports to your Adiuvo account about a connected site.

0.2.0

  • Security: the site refuses ADI over plain http, and a site without https cannot create a connection, so a token never travels unencrypted. Sites on your own computer (localhost) still work.
  • Security: ADI can no longer save a tag left unfinished at the end of a field, or comment-like markup that browsers and WordPress read differently. Either could slip an event handler past the rule that keeps scripts out. Markup already on a page stays as it is.
  • Security: deleting a WordPress user revokes that user’s connections.
  • Security: nothing can switch off the rule that keeps scripts, embeds (iframes), forms and event handlers from being added through ADI. The developer filter adi_bridge_allow_unsafe_markup, which could, is gone.
  • The settings screen (Settings → ADI Bridge) can be translated.
  • Messages are written to the PHP error log only when the site’s debug log is on (WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG).
  • The readme lists the external services ADI uses, with an FAQ.

0.1.4

  • Two changes to the same page at the same moment are saved one after the other, so neither can undo the other, and “only if it still holds what I read” now holds under load.
  • Undoing ADI’s last change (while nothing else on the page has changed) puts the page back exactly, including harmless markup pasted from a chat app that ADI itself never adds. Scripts, embeds, forms, buttons, inputs, event handlers and script links are still never put back through ADI.
  • Changes through ADI can no longer add data-* attributes that script libraries run code from (htmx, Datastar, Bootstrap toggles…), code-like data-* values, page-covering positioned elements, or links whose real address is a script once entities are decoded. Plain data-* values (a booking widget’s link, a gallery id) stay editable.

0.1.3

  • Connects on hosts that remove the standard Authorization header before WordPress sees it. Needs the latest ADI.

0.1.2

  • WooCommerce: edit simple products’ regular and sale prices (shown with the store currency), sale dates, SKU and stock; assign existing categories and tags; set the product image and gallery from the Media Library; edit simple products’ own attribute values.
  • WooCommerce variable products: edit each variation’s prices, sale dates, SKU, stock, enabled/disabled status and image; the product’s price range updates automatically. Variations are never added or removed.
  • Every WooCommerce change keeps a restore point; stock is only put back from a restore point taken for a stock change, because orders change stock in between.
  • Store settings (currency, tax, shipping), orders, customers, coupons and payments are never changed.

0.1.1

  • Security: no connection can add scripts, embeds (iframes), forms, event handlers or links other than http(s), mailto and tel, whatever its WordPress role; markup already on a page stays as it is. A stolen connection token can still change text, but can no longer add code (scripts or embeds) to the site.
  • Security: a restore puts back only what ADI itself edits (field values, Elementor content, featured image), leaving other plugins’ data alone.
  • The connection tells ADI that site content is data, never instructions.
  • Settings → ADI Bridge warns when a connection is created for an administrator; an Editor is recommended.
  • Error messages no longer include database error text.

0.1.0

  • First release: MCP endpoint, connection tokens, Classic / Block editor / Elementor / ACF editing, restore points, cache purging, SEO protection.
